issues.title: 'Go aims to be a steady hand on the tiller.'
issues.html:
#​624 — November 13, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





Go Turns 17: An Update — A mini 'State of the Union' to celebrate Go's 17th birthday (first unveiled in a quite understated post in 2009). Austin recaps a year of Go improvements, but also looks ahead to 2027 with (a large subset of) SIMD graduating in 1.28, cutting Go's memory footprint "amid the global RAM crunch", and a reworked proposal process that will involve the Go community more.

Austin Clements (Go Team)



19 of 57 AI APIs Still Make You Poll for Job Results — That’s one finding in the State of Webhooks 2027. We scored 489 API companies, 66 of them AI API providers, against 17 criteria, from retries and signatures to how well agents can build on their events. Immediate download, no email required.

Svix sponsor



Inside PGO: What Go's Compiler Does With Your Profile — An illustrated dive behind the scenes of how Go's profile guided optimization feature operates. PGO is essentially a way to let the compiler optimize your app based on how it runs by inlining hot calls, aligning hot loops, and more.

Jesús Espino



💡 Lamplit Labs measured PGO on a log router and found 8.8-10% fewer instructions per line, all of it from inlining.



IN BRIEF:

  • 🔐 Go 1.27.4 and 1.26.11 have been released with twelve security fixes. Most of them prevent a malicious cgo dependency from running code at build time, and the stricter checks mean --sysroot and -target are no longer allowed in #cgo directives.

  • Go's new experimental generic collection types are ready to try in golang.org/x/exp/collection: sets, hashed maps, and the newly accepted sorted maps and sets. The Go team hopes to add them to the standard library in 1.29.

  • Austin Clements has proposed graduating a large subset of simd and simd/archsimd out of their experiment for Go 1.28, covering AMD64, ARM64 NEON, and WebAssembly.

  • Publishing the analyzer API as a go/analysis package in the standard library is now a 'likely accept', paving the way for go test to run your project's own analyzers.

  • ✈️ Tinyflight is TinyGo-based flight control firmware for the M5Stack StampFly 'mini quadcopter' (that you can also fly in a browser simulator here).



Catch Go Bugs That Fuzzing Misses with Gemini and a Constraint Solver — A delightfully technical post on Google's dev blog that highlights a shortcoming in Go's fuzzer where slice overruns can be missed (though a simple tweak can expose them), and experiments with a way to use Gemini and Z3 to find them directly.

Karl Weinmeister (Google)



CodeAF: 16 Coding Sessions in Half a Gigabyte, Written in Go — Each extra session adds 27 MB of RAM, 8x less than Claude Code. #1 of ten harnesses on DeepSWE, lowest cost per solve.

CodeAF by AgentField AI sponsor



📄 Go's JSON v1 vs v2 Under Load – MarshalWrite's many small writes cut one API's read throughput by 30%. Huseyin Babal

📄 Slashing a Go Service's Memory Use – Swapping map[string]bool sets for sorted []uint64 slices helped cut heap use by 78%. Ed Crewe

📄 A Hands-On Tour of What encoding/json/v2 Changes Christian Ekrem



🛠 Code & Tools





  • Lip Gloss 2.1 – Charm's terminal styling library. Tables can now size themselves to their content while still respecting a maximum width (as above).

  • Iris v14 – The veteran web framework's first major release since v12 now requires Go 1.27 so it can lean on generic methods.

  • checkescape – An introduction to gVisor's analyzer for enforcing zero allocations in annotated functions, à la the recently featured noalloc.

  • codemap – Generates a single interactive HTML visualization of a Go module's packages, dependencies, files, and functions.

  • ws 1.5 – The tiny, low-level WebSocket library adds SIMD-accelerated payload masking and stops trusting peer-declared payload lengths when allocating.

  • go-sqlite3 0.37 – cgo-free SQLite wrapper. database/sql transactions now default to BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

  • Fiber 3.7 – The Express-inspired web framework can now bind map fields from queries and forms.



📰 Classifieds



Billions of rows, one Postgres: TimescaleDB keeps your Go service’s analytics fast without a second database. $1000 credit on Tiger Cloud.

WarpBuild remote docker builders only rebuild what changed with optimized caching beyond just container layers. Get $50 in free credits with code START50.



📊  Go by the Numbers





Alongside Go's 17th birthday, JetBrains has published The State of Go in 2026, covering the results from developers who replied to its annual ecosystem survey and chose Go as one of their main languages. Among the stats for the Go-using respondents:

  • On the editor/IDE front, 14% are now using Zed, up nearly 3x from last year, with GoLand (49%) and VS Code (48%) neck and neck (though remember this is JetBrains' own survey :-)

  • 🤖 86% are using AI coding agents in the terminal on at least a weekly basis (versus 74% for all respondents, including non Go devs), with 55% saying most of their work code in the last month was generated by AI.

  • 46% now use net/http for web development, up from 32% a year ago and almost level with Gin (48%). chi (15%), Echo (13%), and Fiber (13%) follow.

  • 43% use TypeScript alongside Go in the same project, up from 24% in 2024. A Go backend with a TypeScript frontend is becoming de rigueur.

  • 25% say they've used Rust in the past year, but 70% have no plans to move away from Go. 🎉

There's a lot more than that in there, though, so… enjoy!

issues.title: The Go team explains Go's new JSON API
issues.html:
#​623 — November 6, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





The Official Guide to encoding/json/v2 (and Migrating to It) — Now that encoding/json/v2 and jsontext are stable, the Go team has a refreshed introduction to how they work, including how v1 and v2 interoperate. There's also a new migration guide which shows off jsonsplit for running v1 and v2 side by side in production and logging any differences.

Pratt, Tsai, Martí et al. (Go Team)



💡 Lleg put v2 to the test and found nine default behavior changes, 10% faster unmarshaling on plain structs, and big perf gains for deeply recursive custom decoders.



What Happens to Your go func() When the Pod Restarts? — Whatever it was doing is gone: you lose the email being sent or the webhook call. Go Event-Driven, the hands-on training from Watermill's authors, starts with goroutines and ends with Go services where data survives a restart. Don’t miss the last cohort this year that opens November 11.

Three Dots Labs sponsor



How //go:embed Works: From Source Files to Binary — A guided tour of how an embedded file travels through the toolchain, with links to the Go source for each step. Along the way, we learn why import _ "embed" is needed, even when you never reference the package.

Ainsley Clark



IN BRIEF:

  • The draft Go 1.28 release notes now list two new go vet checks for unchecked bufio.Scanner and sql.Rows errors, a FlagSet.All iterator, url.MustParse and Landlock support for subprocesses. The release is targeted for February 2027.

  • 🔐 Go 1.27.4 and 1.26.11 are due on November 10 with security fixes to the standard library and toolchain covering twelve CVEs (a lot for a minor release).

  • React framework Next.js has added (in its 'canary' build) experimental route.go handlers where you can write plain net/http-style GET/POST funcs in a route.go file and Next.js will serve them as routes.

  • Following last month's accepted experiment for building cgo code without a C toolchain, a CL in review reimplements runtime/cgo in Go and assembly on every remaining OS and removes the C code entirely.



PROPOSAL UPDATES:

  • maps.Grow has been accepted and may make it into Go 1.28. Redowan Delowar explains why it's useful.

  • unicode/ascii, a package of ASCII-only string functions generic over strings and byte slices, has been proposed, with naming as a sticking point.

  • runtime/bubble, from two Temporal engineers, would build on testing/synctest's bubbles to let a host program run goroutines, channels and select deterministically.

  • math/decimal, an arbitrary-precision decimal type with explicit rounding modes, has been proposed with an implementation already attached.



Go's Generic Collections Proposal Has Been Accepted — We covered the initial plan in July but now the umbrella proposal is accepted, along with set.Set and hash-based Map and Set types. They'll land in golang.org/x/exp/collection first.

The Go Team



Go's GC Can Hit a Wall on 192 Cores — I doubt many of us work with such mammoth systems, but on 192-core amd64 hosts, heap-triggered GC cycles can take 3-4x longer as idle cores pile onto a shared lock-free stack. arm64 already has mitigations for this, and fixes are in review.

Nate Watson et al.



Is Your Go Service Ready for AI Agents? Run the Free POKE Audit — A free agent skill that audits your Go service and gives the smallest steps to add an event log, SSE, and webhooks.

Svix sponsor



📄 The MustCreate Pattern for Go Tests – How a generic MustCreate(t, NewUsername, "joe123") can replace a pile of per-type test helpers. Michael Lynch

📄 The Heap Profile Named a Function I Didn't Write – alloc_space measures churn, inuse_space what's still live, which can point to different allocation hotspots. Nolan Keir

📄 Sandboxing Subprocesses with Landlock in Go 1.28 – How Go 1.28 will make it easier to restrict subprocesses on Linux. Mohammad Abdolirad

📄 Five Go Exercises Worth Trying – Picks from the practice-go challenge collection, each with a solution walkthrough. Alex Pliutau



🛠 Code & Tools





GoLand 2026.3: Coding Agents Move Into the Go IDE — JetBrains Air is a system for running existing terminal coding agents (like Claude or Codex) within IDEs, and it's now included in JetBrains' Go IDE. A redesigned Home window and Git worktree improvements round out the release.

Artem Pronichev (JetBrains)



go-yaml v4: The First Stable Release Under the YAML Org — The archived gopkg.in/yaml.v3 now has a stable successor, adding Load and Dump functions that take options, a plugin system, and a debugging CLI. Dump's formatting defaults differ from Marshal's, and v2 and v3 now get security fixes only.

The YAML Organization



🔎 Betterleaks: A Secrets Scanner from the Creator of Gitleaks — The creator of Gitleaks no longer controls that project, so this is its successor, written in Go. It scans Git history, GitHub/GitLab orgs, S3 and container images, and can check whether found keys are still active.

Zach Rice et al.



Fanout: A Single-Binary OpenTelemetry Backend in Go — From the creator of Echo: OTLP in, Parquet on disk, DuckDB for queries, all in one Go binary. It's alpha, but could be an appealing alternative to a full observability stack for smaller setups. GitHub repo.

Vishal Rana



📰 Classifieds



Billion-row analytics with plain database/sql: TimescaleDB extends Postgres, so your Go code doesn’t change. Get $1000 credit.

WarpBuild provides optimized hardware and fast Golang caches for CI. At half the cost. Get $50 in free credits with code START50.



  • 🔒 pgx 5.12 – The Postgres driver fixes a SQL injection in simple-protocol batches and a require_auth bypass. It also adds batched transaction startup, client certificate policy controls, and per-query batch timing.

  • Wails 3.1 – An update after last week's big 3.0 release with fixes, performance improvements, and experimental cgo-free macOS and Linux backends.

  • 🤖 ADK for Go 2.7 – Google's agent toolkit adds Claude as a first-party (experimental) model option and experimental classifiers for workflow routing.

  • Excelize 2.11.1 – The spreadsheet reading/writing library tackles 16 CVEs, mostly crashes and runaway allocations on malicious input, and now requires Go 1.26+.

  • Ginkgo 2.34 – The BDD-style test framework adds DeferOnFailure for capturing state before teardown destroys it.

issues.title: Wails 3 arrives after nearly four years
issues.html:
#​622 — October 30, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





Wails 3.0: Build Desktop Apps with Go and Native Web Views — Nearly four years after its alpha, Wails 3 lets you build desktop apps with a Go backend and web frontend, rendered in a native WebView. 3.0 adds multiple windows, system tray support, an in-app updater, and generated JavaScript and TypeScript bindings for Go services. Mobile support remains experimental.

Lea Anthony



Stop Hand-Rolling Webhooks in Your Go Service — Your webhooks want one package, one call per event, and idiomatic Go with typed models. Svix handles retries, signing, delivery logs, and a portal for your customers, so you don’t build any of it. Clerk has run its webhooks on Svix for 3+ years.

Svix sponsor



How Go Shipped Its First URGENT Track Security Release — As featured last week, Go hardcoded a block on eMudhra's broken intermediate certs. Now the Go security team explains why the notes were vague, how the fix shipped hours after they were alerted, and its plan for revocation checking on Linux.

Roland Shoemaker (Go Team)



IN BRIEF:

  • 🔒 golang.org/x/net v0.62.0 fixes two bugs in its html package: a quadratic slowdown on crafted input and a raw text rendering flaw.

  • Filippo Valsorda has proposed friendlier crypto/aead packages for symmetric encryption, plus crypto/cobblestone for messages too big to hold in memory.

  • 𝕏 Emma Twersky, familiar to many from Angular's DevRel team, now leads Frameworks and Languages DevRel at Google, covering Go alongside Flutter and Dart.



🔒 Go on Linux and CVE-2026-98432: Patch Your Kernel — Go enables Multipath TCP by default for listeners in apps whose main module declares go 1.24 or later. Anthropic's remote root exploit for a new Linux kernel bug used such a listener, but the bug isn't MPTCP-specific. Update your kernel, as GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0 is only "a fragile mitigation".

Neal Patel (Go Security Team)



💡 An issue that proposes Go turn the default off is open, but the Go team says any change would be premature for now. The issue is ultimately with Linux, not Go.



Go Concurrency Distilled — A handy interactive refresher where Anton boils Go's numerous concurrency concepts and mechanisms down into a single page, covering everything from channels and select to context, synctest and the scheduler, with examples you can edit and run in place.

Anton Zhiyanov



📊 Measuring Go 1.28's HTTP/2 'Parking' Memory Savings — Thanks to a change by Brad Fitzpatrick, an idle HTTP/2 server connection in Go 1.28 can let its serve goroutine exit. With 5,000 idle connections, a dev build ran 5,000 fewer goroutines and used about 40% less RSS.

Mohammad Abdolirad



Proposal: Let go test Run Your Project's Own Analyzers — //go:analyze directives would add custom analyzers to go test, and libraries could ship checks that run on packages that import them, like vet checks Printf calls. It's still early but being actively discussed.

Alan Donovan (Go Team)



📺 Profiling Go with pprof: Flame Graphs and Memory Leaks – A quick, six minute primer that finds a CPU hog and leak in an app. Hüseyin Babal

📄 Partial Updates in Go with Field Masks – How to separate update intent from values in PATCH requests. Redowan Delowar

📄 Where Go 1.27's HTTP/1 Connection Reuse Stops Working Lleg



🛠 Code & Tools





gohawk: Static Analysis for Leaks and Lock Bugs — Finds leaked files, unjoined goroutines, unreaped processes and lock inversions, using Infer-style function summaries to track ownership across packages. It's a young project, but has already led to merged fixes in Moby and Caddy. (GitHub repo.)

James Ko



TinyGo 0.44: Smaller, Faster, Better — The Go compiler for microcontrollers and WebAssembly now does more init work at compile time for smaller binaries that start faster, drops needless slice bounds checks, and adds multicore goroutines on the ESP32-S3. Support for the Arduino Uno R4 also brings TinyGo's first Renesas CPU support.

The TinyGo Team



You Chose Go for Simplicity. Keep Your Data Stack Simple Too — TimescaleDB extends Postgres with compression and continuous aggregates. Your Go code doesn’t change. Get $1000 credit.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



noalloc: Keep Your Hot Paths Allocation-Free — Mark a function with //noalloc:root and this CLI checks its call tree for heap allocations, flagging offending lines. It's a days-old, AI-written experiment that borrows an idea from OxCaml's zero_alloc.

Phil Eaton (The Consensus)



  • 🔒 Echo 5.4.4 – The popular web framework has had four patch releases in eight days, including a fix for a critical access control bypass in its proxy middleware's WebSocket handling.

  • go-json 0.12 – Fast encoding/json-compatible library. Adds a jsontext package and an early encoding/json/v2-style API.

  • cel-go 0.33 – Google's Common Expression Language for Go gets an opt-in parser that's 8-19x faster.

  • Huma 2.40 – Framework for building HTTP APIs with OpenAPI 3 specs.

  • mockery 3.9 – The popular mock generator for Go interfaces. (Docs.)



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • ✨ Richard Seroter, Google Cloud's Chief Evangelist and the exec with product and engineering responsibility for Go, 𝕏 says Go has just become the most-used language on Google Cloud by raw SDK API requests, with Java not far behind.

  • Before 'distributed SQLite' became a busy, venture-funded category, there was rqlite, built in Go in 2014. Its creator tells the story of the ecosystem's growth.

  • Lisette is a Rust-inspired language with algebraic data types, pattern matching and no nil that compiles to readable Go and can call Go packages directly.

  • ⚠️ A reminder that the 2026 Go Developer Survey closes for submissions on November 3, so there are a few more days to have your say.
